risk.title: Does a fragile world lose more?
risk.caption: Every game from iteration 500 on of the 30 worlds. x: after the game's unused connections are cut, just before the cull, the largest share of the world that one bridge held to the rest — if that one connection were cut, that many would be cut off ([Cut risk](bridges.md#cut-risk)). y: the share of agents the game really cut off. White: the mean of y in classes of x 0.05 wide; dashed: y = x.
risk.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`.

**Data.** From each run's `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/stats.jsonl`, which holds one row per recorded phase: `phase` 1 is the world just after reproduction, `phase` 2 just after the game, and every statistic is a field of the row (see [What a run records](frames-and-stats.md)).

1. Take the rows with `phase` = 2 and 500 ≤ `iteration` ≤ 1,499: `cutRiskBefore`, and `orphaned` / `nodes_before`.
2. Plot one against the other; average y in classes of x.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py breaking`.

deaths-by-size.title: Where the cut-off deaths happen
deaths-by-size.caption: Of all agents cut off in games from iteration 500 on of the 30 worlds, the share that died in games which cut off at least n agents, for every n. Where the line is at 0.5, half of all such deaths happened in games at least that large.
deaths-by-size.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`.

**Data.** From each run's `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/stats.jsonl`, which holds one row per recorded phase: `phase` 1 is the world just after reproduction, `phase` 2 just after the game, and every statistic is a field of the row (see [What a run records](frames-and-stats.md)).

1. Take `orphaned` of the rows with `phase` = 2 and 500 ≤ `iteration` ≤ 1,499.
2. For every n, add up `orphaned` over the rows with `orphaned` ≥ n and divide by the total.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py breaking`.

one-world.title: 600 iterations of one world
one-world.caption: The world with seed 26, iterations 600 to 1,200. Top: its number of agents after every game. Middle: how many agents each game cut off. Bottom: before each game, the largest share of the world held to the rest by a single bridge, measured on the network as it stood before the cleanup.
